# Information Security Standard: Access Control and Authentication

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This standard establishes requirements for access control and authentication controls at Acme Health. All systems that process, store, or transmit organizational information must comply with the requirements specified herein.

## 2. Policy and Procedures Management

### 2.1 Identification and Authentication Policy

Acme Health must develop, document, and disseminate an [Selection (one or more): organization-level; mission/business process-level; system-level] identification and authentication policy to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] that: (a) addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and (b) is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. [NIST 800-53 IA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must develop, document, and disseminate procedures to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] to facilitate the implementation of the identification and authentication policy and the associated identification and authentication controls. [NIST 800-53 IA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the identification and authentication policy and procedures. [NIST 800-53 IA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory]

### 2.2 Policy and Procedures Review and Update

Acme Health must review and update the identification and authentication policy at least every one year and following [Assignment: organization-defined events], or [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events] where a different frequency is specified. [NIST 800-53 IA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must review and update the identification and authentication procedures at least every one year and following [Assignment: organization-defined events], or [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events] where a different frequency is specified. [NIST 800-53 IA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory]

### 2.3 Documentation Maintenance and Availability

Acme Health must maintain policies and procedures in written (which may be electronic) form, and retain for 6 years from the date of creation or the date when last in effect, whichever is later. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(1) | HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(i)]

Acme Health must make documentation available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(ii)]

Acme Health must review documentation periodically, and update as needed, in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(iii)]

## 3. Account Lockout Controls

### 3.1 Invalid Logon Attempt Limits

[Identity Provider] must enforce a limit of five consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a 15-minute time period, or enforce a limit of [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a [Assignment: organization-defined time period] where specific values are not defined. [NIST 800-53 AC-7 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

### 3.2 Account Lockout Actions

[Identity Provider] must automatically lock the account or node for a minimum of 30 minutes, lock until released by an administrator, delay next logon prompt per [Assignment: organization-defined delay algorithm], notify system administrator, or take other [Assignment: organization-defined action] when the maximum number of unsuccessful logon attempts is exceeded. [NIST 800-53 AC-7 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

### 3.3 Mobile Device Purge or Wipe

[Mobile Device Management System] must purge or wipe information from mobile devices after 10 consecutive unsuccessful device logon attempts based on [Assignment: organization-defined purging or wiping requirements and techniques]. [NIST 800-53 AC-7(2) | ARC-AMPE AC-7(2) AE Mandatory]

### 3.4 Biometric Authentication Limits

Systems supporting biometric authentication must limit the number of unsuccessful biometric logon attempts to [Assignment: organization-defined number]. [NIST 800-53 AC-7(3)]

### 3.5 Alternative Authentication Factors

Systems must allow use of [Assignment: organization-defined authentication factors] that are different from the primary authentication factors after the number of consecutive invalid logon attempts have been exceeded, and enforce a limit of [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive invalid logon attempts through use of the alternative factors by a user during a [Assignment: organization-defined time period]. [NIST 800-53 AC-7(4)]

## 4. System Use Notification

### 4.1 System Use Notification Display

Systems must display [Assignment: organization-defined system use notification message or banner] to users before granting access to the system that provides privacy and security notices consistent with applicable laws, Executive Orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines and states that: (1) users are accessing a U.S. Government system or a system that contains U.S. Government information; (2) system usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit; (3) unauthorized use of the system is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties; and (4) use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording. [NIST 800-53 AC-8 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

Systems must retain the notification message or banner on the screen until users acknowledge the usage conditions and take explicit actions to log on to or further access the system. [NIST 800-53 AC-8 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

### 4.2 Publicly Accessible Systems

For publicly accessible systems: (1) systems must display system use information [Assignment: organization-defined conditions] before granting further access; (2) systems must display references, if any, to monitoring, recording, or auditing that are consistent with privacy accommodations for such systems that generally prohibit those activities; and (3) systems must include a description of the authorized uses of the system. [NIST 800-53 AC-8 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

### 4.3 System Use Notification Verification

Acme Health must determine elements of the environment that require system use notification, how system use notification will be verified, and provide appropriate periodicity of the verification check. [ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

## 5. Concurrent Sessions

### 5.1 Session Limits

Systems must limit the number of concurrent sessions for each [Assignment: organization-defined account and/or account types] to one session, or to [Assignment: organization-defined number] where a different limit is specified. [NIST 800-53 AC-10 High | ARC-AMPE AC-10 AE Mandatory]

### 5.2 Documentation of Concurrent Session Requirements

Acme Health must document any requirement for more than one concurrent application/process session in the applicable security and privacy plan. [ARC-AMPE AC-10 AE Mandatory]

## 6. Device Lock

### 6.1 Device Lock Activation

Systems must prevent further access to the system by initiating a device lock after 15 minutes of inactivity or [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of inactivity, or by requiring the user to initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended. [NIST 800-53 AC-11 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-11 AE Mandatory]

Systems must retain the device lock until the user reestablishes access using established identification and authentication procedures. [NIST 800-53 AC-11 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-11 AE Mandatory]

### 6.2 Device Lock Display

Systems must conceal, via the device lock, information previously visible on the display with a publicly viewable image. [NIST 800-53 AC-11(1) Moderate, High]

### 6.3 Workstation Security

Acme Health must implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of specific workstations or classes of workstations that can access electronic protected health information. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.310(b)]

## 7. Session Management

### 7.1 Automatic Session Termination

Systems must automatically terminate a user session after [Assignment: organization-defined conditions or trigger events requiring session disconnect]. [NIST 800-53 AC-12 Moderate, High | HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(a)(2)(iii) | ARC-AMPE AC-12 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must define conditions or trigger events requiring session disconnect in the applicable security and privacy plans, which may include organization-defined periods of user inactivity, targeted responses to certain types of incidents, or time-of-day restrictions on system use. [ARC-AMPE AC-12 AE Mandatory]

### 7.2 User-Initiated Session Logout

Systems must provide a logout capability for user-initiated communications sessions whenever authentication is used to gain access to [Assignment: organization-defined information resources]. [NIST 800-53 AC-12(1) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(1) AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must define information resources requiring logout capability in the applicable security and privacy plans. [ARC-AMPE AC-12(1) AE Mandatory]

### 7.3 Logout Message Display

Systems must display an explicit logout message to users indicating the termination of authenticated communications sessions. [NIST 800-53 AC-12(2) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(2) AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must document an organization-defined standard logout message in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP). [ARC-AMPE AC-12(2) AE Mandatory]

### 7.4 Session Timeout Warning

Systems must display an explicit message to users indicating that the session will end in [Assignment: organization-defined time until end of session]. [NIST 800-53 AC-12(3) | ARC-AMPE AC-12(3) AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must specify the organization-defined time until end of session in the applicable security and privacy plans. [ARC-AMPE AC-12(3) AE Mandatory]

## 8. User Identification and Authentication

### 8.1 Organizational User Authentication

Systems must uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users and associate that unique identification with processes acting on behalf of those users. [NIST 800-53 IA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-2 | ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must employ effective identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63, Digital Identity Guidelines document suite. [ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory]

Systems must require the use of system and/or network authenticators and unique user identifiers for organizational users. [ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory]

[Ticketing System] must require user identification for any help desk transaction that has information security and privacy implications. [ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory]

### 8.2 Multi-Factor Authentication for Privileged Accounts

Systems must implement multi-factor authentication for access to privileged accounts. [NIST 800-53 IA-2(1) Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-2(1) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(1) AE Mandatory]

Multi-factor authentication for privileged accounts must be phishing-resistant in accordance with current CISA guidance. [FedRAMP IA-2(1)]

Multi-factor authentication for privileged accounts must use two or more different factors: something you know (e.g., a personal identification number), something you have (e.g., a physical authenticator such as a cryptographic private key), or something you are (e.g., a biometric). [ARC-AMPE IA-2(1) AE Mandatory]

### 8.3 Multi-Factor Authentication for Non-Privileged Accounts

Systems must implement multi-factor authentication for access to non-privileged accounts. [NIST 800-53 IA-2(2) Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-2(2) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(2) AE Mandatory]

Multi-factor authentication for non-privileged accounts must be phishing-resistant in accordance with current CISA guidance. [FedRAMP IA-2(2)]

While multi-factor authentication is not currently mandated for consumer accounts, it is strongly recommended; MFA is required for all other non-privileged account types. [ARC-AMPE IA-2(2) AE Mandatory]

### 8.4 Shared Account Authentication

When shared accounts or authenticators are employed, systems must require users to be individually authenticated before granting access to the shared accounts or resources. [NIST 800-53 IA-2(5) High | ARC-AMPE IA-2(5) AE Mandatory]

### 8.5 Multi-Factor Device Separation

Systems must implement multi-factor authentication for local, network, and remote access to privileged and non-privileged accounts such that: (a) one of the factors is provided by a device separate from the system gaining access; and (b) the device meets [Assignment: organization-defined strength of mechanism requirements] or the latest published FIPS 140-compliant cryptography. [NIST 800-53 IA-2(6) | FedRAMP IA-2(6) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(6) AE Mandatory]

### 8.6 Replay-Resistant Authentication

Systems must implement replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for access to privileged accounts and non-privileged accounts. [NIST 800-53 IA-2(8) Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-2(8) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(8) AE Mandatory]

### 8.7 Single Sign-On

Systems must provide a single sign-on capability for [Assignment: organization-defined system accounts and services]. [NIST 800-53 IA-2(10)]

### 8.8 PIV Credential Acceptance

Systems must accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials. [NIST 800-53 IA-2(12) Low, Moderate, High]

### 8.9 Out-of-Band Authentication

Systems must implement [Assignment: organization-defined out-of-band authentication] mechanisms under [Assignment: organization-defined conditions]. [NIST 800-53 IA-2(13)]

### 8.10 HIPAA User Verification

Acme Health must implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to electronic protected health information is the one claimed. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(d)]

### 8.11 Unique User Identifiers

Systems must assign a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(a)(2)(i)]

### 8.12 Emergency Access

Acme Health must establish (and implement as needed) procedures for obtaining necessary electronic protected health information during an emergency. [HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(a)(2)(ii)]

## 9. Device Identification and Authentication

### 9.1 Device Authentication Requirements

Systems must uniquely identify and authenticate [Assignment: organization-defined devices and/or types of devices] before establishing a [Selection (one or more): local; remote; network] connection, which at a minimum uses shared information (Media Access Control or Internet Protocol address) and access control lists to control remote network access. [NIST 800-53 IA-3 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-3 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must define a list of specific devices and/or types of devices approved and accepted for identification and authentication management in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP). [ARC-AMPE IA-3 AE Mandatory]

### 9.2 Cryptographic Bidirectional Authentication

Systems must authenticate [Assignment: organization-defined devices and/or types of devices] before establishing [Selection (one or more): local; remote; network] connection using bidirectional authentication that is cryptographically based. [NIST 800-53 IA-3(1)]

### 9.3 Dynamic Address Allocation

Where addresses are allocated dynamically, systems must standardize dynamic address allocation lease information and the lease duration assigned to devices in accordance with [Assignment: organization-defined lease information and lease duration], and audit lease information when assigned to a device. [NIST 800-53 IA-3(3)]

### 9.4 Device Attestation

Systems must handle device identification and authentication based on attestation by [Assignment: organization-defined configuration management process]. [NIST 800-53 IA-3(4)]

## 10. Authenticator Management

### 10.1 Authenticator Distribution and Control

Acme Health must verify, as part of the initial authenticator distribution, the identity of the individual, group, role, service, or device receiving the authenticator. [NIST 800-53 IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must establish initial authenticator content for any authenticators issued by the organization. [NIST 800-53 IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must ensure that authenticators have sufficient strength of mechanism for their intended use. [NIST 800-53 IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must establish and implement administrative procedures for initial authenticator distribution, for lost or compromised or damaged authenticators, and for revoking authenticators. [NIST 800-53 IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

### 10.2 Default Authenticator Management

Acme Health must change default authenticators prior to first use. [NIST 800-53 IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

### 10.3 Authenticator Lifecycle Management

Acme Health must change or refresh authenticators [Assignment: organization-defined time period by authenticator type] or when [Assignment: organization-defined events] occur, or when authenticators are no longer valid in the event of known or suspected compromise requiring immediate change, or immediately upon system installation (e.g., default or vendor-supplied passwords). [NIST 800-53 IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must protect authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification. [NIST 800-53 IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

### 10.4 User and Device Authenticator Protection

Acme Health must require individuals to take, and have devices implement, specific controls to protect authenticators, including maintaining possession of authenticators, not sharing authenticators with others, and immediately reporting lost, stolen, or compromised authenticators. [NIST 800-53 IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must change authenticators for group or role accounts when membership to those accounts changes. [NIST 800-53 IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

### 10.5 NIST Authenticator Compliance

Acme Health must comply with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B for authenticator requirements. [ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

Organizational System/User Account passwords must be paired with the use of multi-factor authentication (MFA) solutions; it is strongly recommended that Organizational ACA Consumer Account passwords are paired with the use of MFA solutions. [ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

It is strongly recommended organizations enforce a policy requiring Organizational System/User Account passwords be changed or refreshed at least once every six months. [ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

### 10.6 Password-Based Authentication

For password-based authentication: (a) [Identity Provider] must maintain a list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords and update the list using a frequency defined in applicable security/privacy plans but not to exceed one year, or [Assignment: organization-defined frequency], and when organizational passwords are suspected to have been compromised directly or indirectly. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

For password-based authentication: (b) systems must verify, when users create or update passwords, that the passwords are not found on the list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords in IA-5(1)(a). [NIST 800-53 IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

For password-based authentication: (c) systems must transmit passwords only over cryptographically-protected channels. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

For password-based authentication: (d) systems must store passwords using an approved salted key derivation function, preferably using a keyed hash. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

For password-based authentication: (e) systems must require immediate selection of a new password upon account recovery. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

For password-based authentication: (f) systems must allow user selection of long passwords and passphrases, including spaces and all printable characters. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

For password-based authentication: (g) systems must employ automated tools to assist the user in selecting strong password authenticators. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

For password-based authentication: (h) systems must enforce the following composition and complexity rules: [Assignment: organization-defined composition and complexity rules], or ensure password composition and complexity complies with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B with ACA Consumer Accounts having a minimum of eight characters, Administrator/Privileged Accounts having a minimum of twelve characters, and all other accounts having a minimum of eight characters. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

The use of passphrases is strongly recommended to increase password strength; names and words that can be found within a dictionary are not to be used as passwords. [ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

Use of temporary passwords should trigger an immediate change to a permanent password; password lifetime restrictions do not apply to temporary passwords. [ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

### 10.7 Public Key-Based Authentication

For public key-based authentication: (a) systems must enforce authorized access to the corresponding private key and map the authenticated identity to the account of the individual or group; and (b) when public key infrastructure (PKI) is used: (1) systems must validate certificates by constructing and verifying a certification path to an accepted trust anchor, including checking certificate status information; and (2) systems must implement a local cache of revocation data to support path discovery and validation. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(2) Moderate, High]

### 10.8 In-Person or Trusted Third-Party Registration

Acme Health must require developers and installers of system components to provide unique authenticators or change default authenticators prior to delivery and installation. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(5)]

### 10.9 Protection of Authenticators

Acme Health must protect authenticators commensurate with the security category of the information to which use of the authenticator permits access. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(6) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(6) AE Mandatory]

### 10.10 No Embedded Unencrypted Static Authenticators

Acme Health must ensure that unencrypted static authenticators are not embedded in applications or other forms of static storage. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(7) | ARC-AMPE IA-5(7) AE Mandatory]

### 10.11 Multiple System Account Management

Acme Health must implement [Assignment: organization-defined security controls] to manage the risk of compromise due to individuals having accounts on multiple systems. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(8)]

### 10.12 Federated Credential Management

Acme Health must use [Assignment: organization-defined external organizations] to federate credentials. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(9)]

### 10.13 Dynamic Credential Binding

Systems must bind identities and authenticators dynamically using [Assignment: organization-defined binding rules]. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(10)]

### 10.14 Biometric Authentication Quality

For biometric-based authentication, systems must employ mechanisms that satisfy [Assignment: organization-defined biometric quality requirements]. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(12)]

### 10.15 Cached Authenticator Management

Systems must prohibit the use of cached authenticators after [Assignment: organization-defined time period]. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(13)]

### 10.16 PKI Trust Store Management

For PKI-based authentication, Acme Health must employ an organization-wide methodology for managing the content of PKI trust stores installed across all platforms, including networks, operating systems, browsers, and applications. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(14)]

### 10.17 GSA-Approved Products and Services

Acme Health must use only General Services Administration-approved products and services for identity, credential, and access management. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(15)]

### 10.18 In-Person or Trusted Third-Party Issuance

Acme Health must require that the issuance of [Assignment: organization-defined types of and/or specific authenticators] be conducted [Selection: in person; by a trusted external party] before [Assignment: organization-defined registration authority] with authorization by [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(16)]

### 10.19 Biometric Presentation Attack Detection

Systems must employ presentation attack detection mechanisms for biometric-based authentication. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(17)]

### 10.20 Password Manager Use

Acme Health must employ [Assignment: organization-defined password managers] to generate and manage passwords, and protect the passwords using [Assignment: organization-defined controls]. [NIST 800-53 IA-5(18)]

### 10.21 FedRAMP Authenticator Requirements

Authenticators must be compliant with the most recent NIST Digital Identity Guidelines: IAL, AAL, FAL level 1 for FedRAMP Certification Class B; IAL, AAL, FAL level 2 for FedRAMP Certification Class C; or IAL, AAL, FAL level 3 for FedRAMP Certification Class D. [FedRAMP IA-5]

Authentication assertions must be encrypted when passed through third parties, such as a browser (e.g., a SAML assertion can be encrypted using XML-Encryption, or an OpenID Connect ID Token can be encrypted using JSON Web Encryption). [FedRAMP IA-5]

## 11. Authenticator Feedback

Systems must obscure feedback of authentication information during the authentication process to protect the information from possible exploitation and use by unauthorized individuals. [NIST 800-53 IA-6 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-6 AE Mandatory]

## 12. Cryptographic Module Authentication

Systems must implement mechanisms for authentication to a cryptographic module that meet the requirements of applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidelines for such authentication. [NIST 800-53 IA-7 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-7 AE Mandatory]

Information systems containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) must use the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards for cryptographic module authentication. [ARC-AMPE IA-7 AE Mandatory]

## 13. Non-Organizational User Authentication

### 13.1 Non-Organizational User Identification

Systems must uniquely identify and authenticate non-organizational users or processes acting on behalf of non-organizational users. [NIST 800-53 IA-8 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must employ effective identity proofing and authentication processes for non-organizational users compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63, Digital Identity Guidelines document suite; identity proofing and authentication processes must be compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63-3 Digital Identity Guidelines IAL-2/AAL-2. [ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory]

Systems must require the use of system and/or network authenticators and unique user identifiers for non-organizational users. [ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory]

Help desk support for non-organizational users requires user identification for any transaction that has information security and privacy implications. [ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory]

### 13.2 PIV Credential Acceptance from Federal Agencies

Systems must accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials from other federal agencies. [NIST 800-53 IA-8(1) Low, Moderate, High]

### 13.3 External Authenticator Acceptance

Systems must accept only external authenticators that are NIST-compliant, and document and maintain a list of accepted external authenticators. [NIST 800-53 IA-8(2) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-8(2) AE Mandatory]

External credentials must be certified as compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63, Digital Identity Guidelines document suite by an approved accreditation authority, and must meet or exceed those guidelines. [ARC-AMPE IA-8(2) AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must use General Services Administration-approved products and services for identity, credential, and access management for external authenticators. [ARC-AMPE IA-8(2) AE Mandatory]

### 13.4 Identity Management Profiles

Systems must conform to [Assignment: organization-defined identity management profiles] for identity management. [NIST 800-53 IA-8(4) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-8(4) AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must utilize identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63, Digital Identity Guidelines document suite to define identity management profiles. [ARC-AMPE IA-8(4) AE Mandatory]

### 13.5 Acceptance of PIV and Federated Credentials

Systems must accept and verify federated or PKI credentials that meet [Assignment: organization-defined policy]. [NIST 800-53 IA-8(5)]

### 13.6 Disassociability

Systems must implement [Assignment: organization-defined measures] to disassociate user attributes or identifier assertion relationships among individuals, credential service providers, and relying parties. [NIST 800-53 IA-8(6)]

## 14. Re-authentication

Systems must require users to re-authenticate when [Assignment: organization-defined circumstances or situations requiring re-authentication] occur. [NIST 800-53 IA-11 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-11 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must define circumstances or situations requiring re-authentication in applicable security/privacy plans; examples include when authenticators or roles change, when security categories of systems change, when the execution of privileged functions occurs, or after a fixed time-period at a minimum. [ARC-AMPE IA-11 AE Mandatory]

## 15. HIPAA-Specific Requirements

### 15.1 Encryption and Decryption

Acme Health must implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information (addressable). [HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(a)(2)(iv)]

---

*This standard must be reviewed and updated in accordance with the policy review requirements specified in Section 2.2. All [Assignment: ...] and [Selection: ...] placeholders must be formally defined and documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plans (SSPP) or other security documentation before implementation.*
